items.title: Randy Sandke interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 10, 1997
items.q: I mean there’s a lot of people — Chick Corea, Herbie Hancock, I mean I would love to play with those people. I don’t know if I ever will

ctx.x: Well you’ve certainly played with a long list of the really established veterans, and they seem to embrace your approach. The World’s Greatest Jazz Band and Benny Carter. Is there a group of people that you really, really look forward to playing with?

Well I feel that like one of the problems that I have is that when I do my own records or these projects which are more modern, that even conceptually I might have an idea of what I want to do but there’s a difference between that and playing every night in a certain context. This is the context I usually find myself in. And again, I love these guys, I love playing the music. But I would also love to play, say, Smitty Smith is doing “The Tonight Show” now but if he weren’t, work with him. I feel like I would grow…

I think that’s a very important thing you mentioned, is that it’s not going to happen in one night. I mean if you played with Chick Corea for one night, it would be a thrill but to play with him for a time would cause you to expand your own vocabulary perhaps.
